data.title: Why Is Geographic Mobility Declining?
data.author: toomuchtodo
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了美国地理流动性下降的原因，重点分析了几种经济解释。首先，人口老龄化使得搬迁成本更高，因为老年人更可能拥有稳定的工作和家庭，搬迁意愿较低。其次，女性全职工作比例上升和男女收入差距缩小，导致双收入家庭增多，这类家庭搬迁的可能性较小。此外，地理上的收入分布变化、城市设施和住房价格的差异也使得搬迁的吸引力下降。研究显示，失业保险可缓解这一趋势，而接近亲属提供的育儿支持也可能影响搬迁决定。数据分析支持了这些解释，例如已婚有子女家庭和房主的跨州搬迁率较低。总体而言，人口结构变化和经济因素共同导致了地理流动性的下降。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：影响人们搬迁以追求工作的因素和搬迁的代价

不同观点：
• **Animats**：认为需要考察工作变动后持续时间的平均值，因为搬迁的成本（包括经济和非经济方面）很高。如果新工作的工作保障存疑，那么搬迁风险很大。引用美国劳工统计局的数据显示，工作 tenure 自2014年以来下降了16%，并质疑是否有更早的数据。

• **rawgabbit**：认为如今搬迁的好处被严重夸大。卖掉家庭住房搬到一个更昂贵的城市，且买不起任何东西，这是不合理的。

• **AStonesThrow**：提到二战后几十年，美国梦往往与离开父母或乡村小镇进入大城市有关。这种城市化趋势和追求独立性的文化导致了搬迁潮。然而，这种“美国梦”也可能带来负面影响，例如离开家庭支持后可能遭遇失败。个人经历表明，一旦在一个理想地点安顿下来，人们可能不再愿意搬迁。

• **eYrKEC2**：认为地理流动性不值得追求，因为改变社交网络和工作带来的不确定性不值得。引用祖父追逐IBM梦想导致父亲频繁更换学校，最终缺乏长期友谊为例，说明搬迁可能导致人际关系的流失。

• **PicassoCTs**：强调搬迁会牺牲整个社交支持网络，而回报往往是可疑的。

• **bediger4000**：认为现代人拥有比过去更多的财产，搬迁变得更加困难。

补充讨论：
- **搬迁的经济与非经济成本**：多个评论提到搬迁不仅仅是经济负担，还涉及到社交网络的丧失和心理压力。
- **文化和社会期望**：AStonesThrow 提到美国社会对独立性和离开家庭的推崇，这种文化背景影响了人们搬迁的决策。
- **历史数据与趋势**：Animats 关注工作 tenure 的历史数据，并试图通过数据分析理解搬迁趋势的变化。
- **个人经历和家庭影响**：eYrKEC2 和 AStonesThrow 都提到了个人和家庭经历对搬迁决策的影响，显示出这种决策的复杂性和个体差异。

争议焦点：搬迁的代价（经济和非经济）与潜在回报之间的权衡。一些人认为回报不值得牺牲，而其他人则可能有不同看法，视个人情况和期望而定。

43990515.article_content:
Why Is Geographic Mobility Declining?
By
Urvi Neelakantan
,
John Bailey Jones
and
Yue Li
Economic Brief
May 2025, No. 25-19
Key Takeaways
In the U.S., people of all ages are moving less than they did 30 years ago. In this article, we describe some of the leading economic explanations for this decline in geographic mobility.
One set of explanations focuses on long-term trends such as population aging and expanding earnings opportunities for women.
Another set of explanations focuses on changes in the geographic distribution of earnings, urban amenities and housing prices.
From covered wagons to rental vans, moving has been an iconic feature of American life. In the past 30 years, however, moving rates have fallen dramatically. In this article, we describe leading economic explanations for the ongoing decline in mobility.
Figure 1 shows a steady decline in interstate migration rates between 1996 and 2024 across all age groups.
1
The figure also shows that moving rates are consistently higher for younger adults (25-34) than for older age groups and that mobility has declined within every age group. Thus, the overall decline in the mobility rate (age 25+) is due to a combination of population aging and mobility falling within every age group.
Enlarge
Some of the explanations for the decline in mobility involve long-term trends — such as population aging or increased earnings opportunities for women — that make moving costlier. Others appeal to changes in the geographic distribution of earnings, urban amenities and housing prices, all of which make moving less rewarding.
An Economic Framework
The explanations we discuss below fit into a widely used economic framework. Most economic models of migration focus on one or more of the following factors:
2
Employment
Earnings
Amenities (such as weather, shopping and dining)
Proximity to family and friends
Housing prices
These models begin with the assumption that individuals and families migrate when the expected benefits of living in new locations (net of moving costs) exceed the expected benefits of remaining in their current locations. They characterize individuals and locations as multidimensional: Individuals may prefer — or have skills better suited to — some jobs rather than others, and employers may offer higher wages for those jobs in one area than in another. People may also differ in the amenities they prefer, while locations may differ in the amenities they offer. These decisions drive migration flows across areas, with wages and/or housing prices mediating the flows.
Demographic Trends in Employment and Earnings
Men and Women
Figure 2 shows that the fraction of women working full time rose from 57 percent in 1996 to 61 percent in 2024, while the share of men working full time fell from 84 percent to 80 percent.
Enlarge
As Figure 3 shows, over the same period, the ratio of women's earnings to men's earnings among those working full time grew by 23 percentage points.
Enlarge
As the earnings and full-time employment rates of women approach those of men, we should expect geographic mobility to fall for a few reasons. First, dual-earner couples with similar incomes would become more common and, as shown in a 2018 working paper, couples with
similar earnings are less likely to relocate
than those with unequal earnings.
3
The paper further estimated that falling wage differences between sexes accounted for over one-third of the drop in family mobility between 1981 and 2012.
Unemployment insurance appears to mitigate this channel. A 2024 working paper estimated that providing unemployment insurance for the trailing spouse — the spouse who gives up a job to accommodate his or her partner's career move —
increased the probability that a household moves
more than 100 miles by 2.7 percentage points.
4
The convergence of earnings and employment between men and women may also increase the need for child care. This in turn could affect geographic mobility by encouraging individuals or couples with children to locate near relatives who can help with child care. For example, a 2024 working paper found that women living within 25 miles of their parents experienced a substantially smaller drop in earnings after having children than those living further away.
5
Our own analysis of the data is consistent with the above-described forces being at play. We run regressions to examine the predictors of moving across states for people aged 35-54. Table 1 reports the results.

data.title: Weaver Codes: Highly Fault Tolerant Erasure Codes for Storage Systems (2005)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为WEAVER码的新型容错纠删码，专为存储系统设计，具有高容错性，特别适用于分布式冗余存储系统（dRAID）。WEAVER码的主要设计特点包括：(a) 数据块和校验块位于同一条带，(b) 限制校验入度，(c) 平衡对称。虽然它不是最大距离可分码（MDS），但在约束校验入度的情况下，具有最佳存储效率。与镜像和Reed-Solomon码相比，WEAVER码在存储效率和计算复杂性之间取得了良好平衡，适用于需要高容错性的长期存档存储和dRAID系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对2005年某事件或话题的评价

不同观点：
• 观点一：2005年是具有转折性意义的一年  
  - 支持者认为2005年在科技和文化方面都有显著进步。例如，YouTube和Reddit等平台的兴起，改变了人们获取信息和互动的方式。  
  - 论据：社交媒体的崛起促进了信息的自由传播和用户的参与，具有深远影响。

• 观点二：2005年的变化被过度夸大  
  - 反对者认为，虽然2005年出现了一些新技术和平台，但其真正的影响在多年后才显现，当年很多创新并未立即改变主流社会。  
  - 论据：很多2005年推出的技术在当时并不成熟，用户接受度有限，因此不能称之为“转折年”。

• 观点三：2005年是全球政治格局变化的开始  
  - 部分评论者指出，2005年的一些国际事件，如中东局势的变化和欧洲一体化的推进，对后续十几年的国际关系产生了影响。  
  - 例子：伊拉克战争持续、伦敦地铁爆炸案等事件标志着全球安全局势的复杂化。

• 观点四：文化现象的重要性被忽视  
  - 有些评论者强调，2005年是流行文化的重要年份，涌现了许多具有持久影响力的影视和音乐作品。  
  - 例子：电影《蝙蝠侠：侠影之谜》和音乐专辑如Kanye West的《Late Registration》都在此后产生了深远影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：2005年是否真的具有历史转折性  
  - 支持者强调技术和社会变革的即时性和革命性。  
  - 反对者则认为这些变化是渐进的，真正的影响在多年后才显现出来。  
  - 争议还涉及对“转折点”的定义，即短期冲击与长期影响的权衡。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：  
  - 评论中有人提到2005年经济变化，特别是全球化加速对各国经济的影响，但未形成主流观点。  
  - 还有评论提及环境问题开始受到更多关注，如气候变化议题逐渐升温。

43991609.article_content:
WEAVER Codes: Highly Fault Tolerant Erasure Codes for Storage Systems
James Lee Hafner
IBM Almaden Research Center
[email protected]
Abstract:
We present the WEAVER codes, new families of simple highly fault
tolerant XOR-based erasure codes for storage systems (with fault
tolerance up to
).  The design features of WEAVER codes are (a)
placement of data and parity blocks on the same strip, (b) constrained
parity in-degree and (c) balance and symmetry.  These codes are in
general not maximum distance separable (MDS) but have optimal storage
efficiency among all codes with constrained parity in-degree.  Though
applicable to RAID controller systems, the WEAVER codes are probably
best suited in dRAID systems (distributed Redundant Arrangement of
Independent Devices).  We discuss the advantages these codes have over
many other erasure codes for storage systems.
1 Introduction
It has become increasingly clear in the storage industry that RAID5
does not provide sufficient reliability against loss of data either
because of multiple concurrent disk losses or disk losses together
with sector losses (e.g., due to medium errors from the disks).  The
reasons are primarily due to the dramatic increase in single disk
capacity together with a fairly constant per-bit error rate.
Additional factors, as mentioned in [
5
], include
increasing number of disks per system, and use of less reliable disks
such as ATA (vs. SCSI).  The cited paper makes the case for double
fault tolerance; by extrapolation, there is (or will be) a need for
higher fault tolerant codes if these trends continue.  Furthermore, as
the industry moves into very long-term archival storage or dRAID
(distributed Redundant Arrangement of Independent Devices) node-based
systems, the need for higher fault-tolerance erasure codes will likely
become more acute.
-way mirroring can clearly be used to provide additional redundancy
in any system, but the storage efficiency (ratio of user data to the
total of user data plus redundancy data) of mirroring is very low.
(We prefer the term ``efficiency'' in storage contexts instead of the
equivalent term ``rate'' which is more suitable for communication
channels.)  On the other hand, codes like Reed-Solomon
(RS) [
14
] provide optimal storage efficiency (that is,
are maximum distance separable, or MDS) and arbitrarily high fault
tolerance, but require special purpose hardware to enable efficient
computation of the finite field arithmetic on which the codes are
based (or, if formulated as a binary XOR code, generally have higher
computational costs and complexities).
Other erasure codes have been proposed for better fault tolerance than
RAID5, but none has emerged as a clear winner even in the RAID
controller market - the industry has not even settled on a
de
facto
standard for
fault tolerance after 40+ years (since RS
codes were first proposed).  We believe no such ``perfect'' code can
exist; every code requires some trade-offs in efficiency, performance
or fault tolerance.
In this paper, we present the WEAVER codes, so called because the
parity/redundancy values are computed by XOR formulas defined by
patterns that weave through the data.  There are three design
principles that characterize WEAVER codes: (a) every strip (stripe
unit) contains both data and parity from the same stripe (we call
these vertical codes because data and parity are arranged together
vertically on each strip), (b) the number of data values that
contribute to each parity value (parity in-degree) is fixed and, most
importantly, is independent of the stripe size (number of strips) and
(c) balance and symmetry.  The second property enables flexibility in
choices of stripe sizes without altering computational costs (in both
XOR and IO).  In addition, it bounds the computational costs of many
operations (e.g., short writes, rebuild).  More details on these
points are given in Section
3
and elsewhere.
The WEAVER codes are designed with balance and symmetry in three
aspects.  First, every parity is constructed from some fixed number of
data values (we call this number the ``parity in-degree'' - as noted,
it is independent of the stripe size).  Second, each data value
contributes to a fixed number of parity values (we call this the
``data out-degree''; it is also independent of the stripe size).  The
data out-degree for WEAVER codes is set to the fault tolerance, the
theoretical minimum number for the given fault tolerance.  For
additional symmetry, some of the codes have the parity in-degree equal
to the data out-degree - this provides a certain duality between data
and parity.  Third, all the code constructions are specified by a
weave-pattern which is repeated by simple rotation of a base
configuration.  That is, they are rotationally symmetric.
We bound the parity in-degree by the fault tolerance to control the
complexity of parity computations and improve other properties such as
localization (see Section
3.1.2
).  There are
undoubtedly other whole fami

data.article_summary: 文章讲述了Airbnb CEO布莱恩·切斯基如何在2023年11月参与OpenAI高层动荡后，受到启发并重新思考Airbnb的未来。切斯基一直希望Airbnb能像亚马逊一样，从短期租房扩展到更多领域。他设想将Airbnb打造成一个提供各种服务的平台，用户可以通过它寻找摄影师、私人教练或厨师等服务。为此，他计划加强身份验证，甚至让Airbnb的个人资料像政府颁发的ID一样可信。切斯基在感恩节期间疯狂记录下自己的想法，最终形成了一份1,500字的文件。他的领导团队对此表示非常兴奋，并计划在未来几个月内逐步实施这一愿景，包括重启2016年推出的本地体验项目，并最终深入发展AI技术，打造一个超级 concierge服务。切斯基的朋友萨姆·阿尔特曼认为，他有望建立一个与谷歌和微软相媲美的大公司。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Airbnb的服务质量、平台问题以及与酒店的对比

不同观点：
• **支持Airbnb的观点**（levocardia）：一些用户认为Airbnb提供了比酒店更好的性价比，尤其是在厨房、洗衣等设施和隐私方面。他们指出，酒店通常无法提供类似的便利，而且位置可能更差。

• **批评Airbnb的观点**（dreamcompiler）：另一部分用户认为Airbnb的核心服务已经变质，酒店在价格、服务和可预测性上都优于Airbnb。此外，酒店的网站通常更容易导航，技术问题较少。

• **对评价系统的批评**（jen729w）：有用户提到Airbnb的评价系统存在问题，房源的照片和实际状况不符，且在给出低评价后会遭到房东的骚扰，试图通过贿赂来提高评分。

• **对Airbnb商业模式的质疑**（pembrook）：有人认为Airbnb过度依赖软件和市场理念，而忽视了实际的 hospitality 体验。他们指出，市场本身并不是用户来到这个平台的原因，而是实际的住宿体验。

• **负面体验和信任问题**（monster_truck）：一些用户分享了他们的负面体验，包括房源状况不佳、退款困难以及房东试图通过不正当手段获取额外费用。这些用户表示不再信任Airbnb，并转向其他平台如Craigslist。

• **对平台管理和隐私的担忧**（neya）：有用户担心Airbnb在隐私保护方面的问题，例如房东安装隐藏摄像头，且平台对此缺乏有效管理。相比之下，酒店提供了更一致的舒适和安全保障。

• **对社区影响的担忧**（margorczynski）：有用户指出Airbnb对社区的社会结构产生了负面影响，例如噪音问题和对当地房价的推动作用，导致本地居民难以负担生活成本。

• **平台上的转售和预订问题**（speedbird）：一些用户发现Airbnb上存在大量转售未预订酒店房间的现象，导致预订体验不佳，并呼吁平台加强管理。

补充讨论：
• **对未来发展的建议**（seydor, bcoates, iambateman）：一些用户建议Airbnb应专注于为房东提供服务，如清洁和维修，而不是扩展到其他领域如体验服务。还有人认为Airbnb应专注于提升住宿体验，而不是试图成为一个“全能应用”。同时，有用户对Airbnb的未来持乐观态度，希望其能找到可持续的商业模式。

争议焦点：
• Airbnb的评价系统是否公正和透明。
• Airbnb是否有效地管理了房源质量和房东行为。
• Airbnb与酒店相比，是否仍然具有性价比和便利性的优势。
• Airbnb的扩展策略是否偏离了其核心业务，导致用户体验下降。

As Brian Chesky
tells it, the reinvention of Airbnb started with the coup at OpenAI. On November 17, 2023, the board of OpenAI
fired
company CEO Sam Altman. His friend Chesky leapt into action—publicly defending his pal on X, getting on the phone with Microsoft’s CEO, and throwing himself into the thick of Altman’s battle to retake OpenAI. Five days later Altman
prevailed
, and Chesky—“I was so jacked up,” he says—turned his buzzing mind to his own company,
Airbnb
.
Thanksgiving weekend was beginning. The Chesky extended family had already held their turkey get-together a week earlier, and the Airbnb CEO had no holiday plan. He was completely alone in his sprawling San Francisco apartment except for Sophie, his golden retriever.
Still wired out of his mind from the cathartic corporate rescue, Chesky began to write. He wanted to bust the company he’d cofounded out of its pigeonhole of short-term home rentals. Amazon, he was fond of pointing out, was first an online bookstore before it became the everything store. Chesky had long believed that Airbnb should expand in a similar way. But things kept getting in the way—dealing with safety
issues
,
fighting regulation
, coping with the existential crisis of a global pandemic. The company was in danger of being tagged with the word that ambitious entrepreneurs dread like the plague:
mature
.
Now Chesky was emboldened to lay out his vision. Home rentals are simply a service, so why stop there? Airbnb could be
the
platform for booking all sorts of services. While other apps cover specific sectors—food delivery, home maintenance, car rides—Chesky figured that Airbnb’s experience in attractively displaying homes, vetting hosts, and responding to crises could make it more trustworthy than competitors and therefore the go-to option for virtually anything.
In a frantic typing spree at the dining room table, on the couch, the bed, and at times in his office, Chesky specced out how he would redesign the Airbnb app. Its users—now at 2 billion—would open up the app not only at vacation time but whenever they needed to find a portrait photographer, a personal trainer, or someone to cook their meals. Chesky reasoned that Airbnb would need to significantly strengthen its identity verification. He even thought he could get people to use the app as a credential, something as respected as a government-issued ID. If he could transform Airbnb into a storefront for real-world services, Chesky thought, he’d catapult his company from a nearly $10-billion-a-year business into one that boasted membership in tech’s pantheon.
Over the next few days, Chesky spilled these thoughts into an Evernote document. “I was basically going from room to room just pouring out this stream-of-consciousness manifesto, like Jack Kerouac writing
On the Road
,” he says, referring to the frenetically produced single roll of teletype paper that catalyzed the beat movement. “I dusted off all my ideas from 2012 to 2016,” Chesky tells me. “I basically said, ‘We’re not just a vacation app—we’re going to be a platform, a community.’” By Friday he had around 10,000 words, “incomprehensible to anyone but me.” He began to refine it, and by the time the weekend was over, Chesky had distilled his document down to 1,500 words.
PHOTOGRAPH: GABRIELA HASBUN
After the holiday, Chesky gathered his leadership team into a conference room. He handed the team copies of his memo à la Jeff Bezos and waited as his direct reports took it in. “Usually when I share ideas, people aren’t bought in,” he says. “But this time, there wasn’t a lot of feedback. People were really excited. And two years later, that document will now be executed with an exacting detail to what I wrote.”
This month, Airbnb will launch the first stage of its more than $200 million reinvention: a panoply of more than 10,000 vendors peddling a swath of services in 260 cities in 30 countries. It is also revitalizing an unsuccessful experiment the company began in 2016: offering bespoke local activities, or what it calls “experiences.” The next stage, launch date unspecified, involves making your profile on Airbnb so robust that it’s “almost like a passport,” as Chesky puts it. After that comes a deep immersion into AI: Inspired by his relationship with Altman, Chesky hopes to build the ultimate agent, a super-concierge who starts off handling customer service and eventually knows you well enough to plan your travel and maybe the rest of your life.
“Brian’s been badly underrated as a tech CEO,” Altman says of his friend. “He's not usually mentioned in the same breath as Larry Page or Bill Gates, but I think he is on a path to build as big of a company.”
That’s a stretch—Airbnb is nowhere near the size of those oligarchic powers. But Chesky was feeling the need for big changes; While impressive, Airbnb’s growth rate doesn’t suggest that the company will soon reach the trillion-dollar heights of Google and Microsoft. “I’m 43 and

data.title: A simple 16x16 dot animation from simple math rules
data.author: andrewrn
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为 "tixy" 的创意编程挑战。参与者需要用不超过32个字符的代码实现有趣的视觉效果或功能，类似于代码高尔夫。页面上的点可以点击以获取更多信息。基本函数模板为 `(t,i,x,y) =>`，其中 `t` 代表时间，`i` 是索引，`x` 和 `y` 是坐标，开发者可以利用这些参数创作出各种图形效果。这是一个鼓励简洁和创意的编程活动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Tixy平台及其类似项目的讨论与创作分享

不同观点：
• **欣赏与喜爱**：
  ◦ 多个用户（如[stankot], [jakegmaths], [Nautman]等）表达了对Tixy的喜爱，并分享了自己创建的动画或互动效果。他们认为Tixy是一个能够激发创造力的工具，尤其适合编程和数学爱好者。
  
• **创作分享**：
  ◦ 用户们积极分享自己使用Tixy制作的作品链接，如[animal531]的“White blood cells attack”、[Reefersleep]的“X Plus Star”等。这些作品展示了Tixy平台上的多样化创作可能性，包括数学函数、时间变量等的应用。
  
• **扩展与启发**：
  ◦ [rpastuszak]提到受到Tixy启发，开发了一个带有可编程笔刷的绘图应用，并提供了技术实现细节。这表明Tixy不仅限于自身平台，还能激发其他项目的开发。
  
• **类似项目比较**：
  ◦ [stankot]提到了自己创建的类似项目Pulsar，以及另一个使用HTML滑块的项目Sliderland，认为这些项目与Tixy有相似的目标，但在发现Tixy之前已经自行开发。这表明Tixy可能在某些功能上与其他项目重叠，但各有特色。

• **简化工具**：
  ◦ [levzettelin]将Tixy比喻为“Shadertoy的简化版”，认为它适合编程新手。这表明Tixy的简单易用使其成为一个很好的学习与创意工具。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节与作者背景**：
  ◦ [agys]提到了Tixy的作者Martin Kleppe及其在JavaScript魔术方面的成就，提供了相关链接。这为Tixy的技术背景提供了更多信息。
  
• **社区与分享**：
  ◦ [asicsp]提到之前在其他平台上有关于Tixy的讨论和模式分享，表明Tixy有一个活跃的用户社区，用户之间会分享和讨论创作。

争议焦点：
• 没有明显的争议，但[levzettelin]将Tixy描述为“Shadertoy for dummies”可能暗示了一种对Tixy简化性质的看法，可能引发对Tixy是否过于简单的讨论。不过，其他用户更多是表达了赞赏，未见对此观点的反驳。

data.title: Working on complex systems: What I learned working at Google
data.author: 0xKelsey
data.article_summary:
《The Coder Cafe：处理复杂系统》一文由Teiva Harsanyi撰写，讨论了复杂系统的概念以及在Google工作期间获得的见解。文章首先区分了“复杂问题”和“繁杂问题”：繁杂问题虽复杂但可预测并有结构化解决方案，而复杂问题则需要适应性和新颖的解决方案。例如，优化打车软件中的司机-乘客匹配属于繁杂问题，而Google的大规模机器学习基础设施则涉及真正的复杂问题。

文章进一步描述了复杂系统的五大特征：
1. **涌现行为**：系统整体行为无法通过单独分析其组成部分预测。
2. **延迟后果**：行动的后果可能不会立即显现，而是延迟出现。
3. **局部与全局优化**：优化某一部分不一定改善整体，有时甚至适得其反。
4. **滞后效应**：系统过去的状态继续影响其行为。

理解这些特征有助于识别和处理复杂系统，避免用解决繁杂问题的方法处理复杂问题，从而更有效地应对挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：复杂系统与复杂性在不同领域和情境下的应用与理解

不同观点：
• **braza** 认为，很多文章没有区分可控复杂性和环境/偶然复杂性。可控复杂性下，实施者对系统有较大控制权，而环境/偶然复杂性则包含很多内在且通常无法解决的限制。他以Google为例，指出尽管Google处理的问题很复杂，但在某些领域（如海运物流、制造业等）由于缺乏数据，这些问题可能更复杂。
• **dmoy** 提到在Google工作的文化，即“不可能的事情变得只是困难，而简单的事情变得困难”。这种文化可能导致对复杂性理解的偏差。
• **RenThraysk** 和 **Pavilion2095** 指出了一个具体的技术问题：网站的cookie政策协议有bug，点击“仅必要”选项后协议会重新出现。这引发了对复杂系统实际应用中的细节问题的关注。
• **ggm** 反驳了两个神话：复杂系统本质上是坏的，以及简单系统总是更好。他以武装部队和供应链为例，说明复杂性有时是必要的，并且简单系统也可能包含隐藏的复杂性。
• **nottorp** 认为，大多数项目 unlikely 达到Google的规模或复杂系统级别，暗示对于大多数开发者来说，讨论Google级别的复杂性可能并不相关。

Hello! Today, let’s discuss a fascinating topic: complex systems.
Introduction
Throughout my career, I’ve worked in many complicated environments. For instance, I worked on optimizing driver-passenger matching in ride-hailing at a Uber's competitor. This context, like others, was technically challenging. Yet, nothing comes close in terms of complexity with my current experience at Google and two years there have refined my perception of complexity.
In this post, we will break down the very concept of complexity. Next, we will take a step back to understand what makes certain environments rather complex than complicated and then explore patterns for navigating complex systems effectively.
Complicated vs. Complex
Understanding the distinction between complicated and complex problems is crucial because each requires a fundamentally different approach:
Complicated problems are intricate but predictable
. They followed structured, repeatable solutions. For example, filing taxes is complicated, but it's a structured and conventional problem since the process remains mostly the same year after year.
Complex problems are intricate but unique
. They require adaptive and often novel solutions. For example, climate change mitigation is a complex problem because it requires new and adaptive solutions and existing methods alone can’t really address its evolving challenges.
Back to software engineering, at the Uber competitor,
one of the challenges was to efficiently find the nearest driver for a passenger
. This was far from trivial, but it wasn't
complex
per se. Indeed, many solutions exist, such as applying geo-hashing (
example
), and implementing one of these solutions was the right approach.
At Google, I work as a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), focusing on the systems powering Google’s ML infrastructure. Here,
I consider the challenges genuinely complex
, as new paradigms and scheduling approaches are required, especially at Google’s scale.
Recognizing whether a system is complicated or complex is really important. Indeed, we mentioned that complicated systems are by definition repeatable, while complex systems require unique and customized approaches. Therefore, if we try to apply a common solution to a complex problem,
it may not lead to effective results
.
Characteristics of Complex Systems
In this section, we will discuss five common characteristics that help identify complex systems. Not all complex systems share every characteristic, but they tend to exhibit at least some of the following.
Emergent Behavior
Emergent behavior arises when a system's overall behavior
cannot be predicted solely by analyzing its individual components in isolation
.
For example, Gemini producing
unexpected results
was an emergent behavior. While I can't disclose the root cause, this behavior was nearly impossible to foresee by analyzing all the different components separately.
This is one possible characteristic of complex systems: they behave in ways that can hardly be predicted just by looking at their parts, making them harder to debug and manage.
Delayed Consequences
Another possible characteristic of complex systems is delayed consequences, where actions
don't always have immediate effects
, and instead, consequences may only become apparent much later.
For example, deploying a new version of a system might introduce a subtle issue that only appears days or even weeks later. This delay complicates debugging since identifying the root cause becomes much harder compared to immediate impacts.
In complex systems, relying solely on immediate feedback can create a false sense of stability, leading to major surprises when an issue finally emerges. Keeping in mind that consequences may take time to surface is essential when working in such environments.
Local vs. Global Optimization
In complex systems,
optimizing one part doesn’t necessarily improve the whole system
, and in some cases, it can even make things worse.
Unlike in non-complex systems, where improving one part generally leads to positive gains, complex systems are much more difficult to reason about. The components interact in non-obvious ways, and local optimizations can create ripple effects that are difficult to predict, sometimes leading to negative outcomes at the system level.
This highlights a key trait of complex systems: the whole is more than the sum of its parts. As a result, local gains don’t always translate into global improvements and in some cases, they can even degrade the overall system.
Hysteresis
Hysteresis describes how a system's
past state continues to influence its behavior
, even after the original cause is removed.

43971177.article_summary:
《The Coder Cafe：处理复杂系统》一文由Teiva Harsanyi撰写，讨论了复杂系统的概念以及在Google工作期间获得的见解。文章首先区分了“复杂问题”和“繁杂问题”：繁杂问题虽复杂但可预测并有结构化解决方案，而复杂问题则需要适应性和新颖的解决方案。例如，优化打车软件中的司机-乘客匹配属于繁杂问题，而Google的大规模机器学习基础设施则涉及真正的复杂问题。

文章进一步描述了复杂系统的五大特征：
1. **涌现行为**：系统整体行为无法通过单独分析其组成部分预测。
2. **延迟后果**：行动的后果可能不会立即显现，而是延迟出现。
3. **局部与全局优化**：优化某一部分不一定改善整体，有时甚至适得其反。
4. **滞后效应**：系统过去的状态继续影响其行为。

理解这些特征有助于识别和处理复杂系统，避免用解决繁杂问题的方法处理复杂问题，从而更有效地应对挑战。

data.title: Lightweight open source reCaptcha alternative
data.author: michalpleban
data.article_summary: ALTCHA 是一个自托管的 CAPTCHA 替代方案，利用工作量证明（PoW）机制保护网站和在线服务免受垃圾信息和滥用。它不依赖 cookies 或指纹识别，确保用户隐私，并符合 GDPR、WCAG 2.2 AA 标准以及欧洲无障碍法案（EAA）。其特点包括无摩擦的用户体验、无 cookie 设计、完全无障碍、轻量级（GZIP 压缩后仅 17 kB）、自托管以及提供 SaaS 选项。安装和使用简单，支持多种前端和后端技术，并可通过配置实现多种功能。与 hCaptcha 和 reCAPTCHA 相比，ALTCHA 的体积更小，性能更优。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕CAPTCHA及相关技术（如PoW）的有效性、实现方式及其潜在问题。

不同观点：
• [binary132] 认为依赖专有托管服务（如CAPTCHA）存在风险，因为这些服务可能会消失或失效。他强调依赖第三方服务不合理，特别是当这些服务可能会轻易中断或取消时。相比之下，专有软件如果能够自行操作和修复，则更有优势。

• [serhack_] 提出有效的CAPTCHA类系统依赖于大量数据收集和模式识别，并根据用户行为动态提供挑战。例如，如果系统识别出疑似机器人，会提供性能较低的PoW挑战。

• [dankobgd] 批评reCAPTCHA不仅无用，还惹恼真实用户，并认为其主要目的是收集用户数据。

• [pabs3] 对PoW系统提出技术疑问，询问如果不设置cookie，系统如何知道用户已计算PoW，是否每次页面加载都需要重新计算。

• [Jleagle] 进一步探讨机器人为何无法计算PoW，暗示可能存在技术上的误解或需要澄清的地方。

• [rahimnathwani] 关心是否有实时演示，显示出对实际应用和文档不足的关注。

• [progx] 提出在人工智能时代，如何区分真实人类和AI的问题，反映了对传统CAPTCHA系统有效性的根本质疑。

• [chrismorgan] 详细分析CAPTCHA的演变和局限，指出其最初目的是区分人类和计算机，但现在已偏离初衷，更多是关于防止滥用。他特别提到PoW机制的潜在缺陷，特别是SHA哈希算法在面对专用硬件时可能无效。

• CAPTCHA系统的有效性和用户体验之间的平衡是争议焦点。部分评论认为CAPTCHA更倾向于收集数据和限制用户，而不是有效防止机器人。
• PoW机制的技术细节及其在安全性与用户体验之间的权衡是另一个值得注意的讨论点，特别是针对其在面对专用硬件时的脆弱性。
• 对现有CAPTCHA替代方案的实际应用和演示的关注，显示出对技术文档和实际效果的期望和质疑。

总体而言，讨论围绕CAPTCHA及其替代方案的技术实现、安全性、用户体验和潜在数据收集问题展开，反映了不同利益相关者对该技术的复杂看法。

43971068.article_summary: ALTCHA 是一个自托管的 CAPTCHA 替代方案，利用工作量证明（PoW）机制保护网站和在线服务免受垃圾信息和滥用。它不依赖 cookies 或指纹识别，确保用户隐私，并符合 GDPR、WCAG 2.2 AA 标准以及欧洲无障碍法案（EAA）。其特点包括无摩擦的用户体验、无 cookie 设计、完全无障碍、轻量级（GZIP 压缩后仅 17 kB）、自托管以及提供 SaaS 选项。安装和使用简单，支持多种前端和后端技术，并可通过配置实现多种功能。与 hCaptcha 和 reCAPTCHA 相比，ALTCHA 的体积更小，性能更优。

data.title: Critical Warning for External Purchases in Apple App Store
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了苹果公司在App Store中对使用外部支付系统的应用显示关键警告的新措施。这些警告会在应用不使用苹果内购（IAP）时出现，并在App Store界面顶部添加多行提示文字，甚至在应用名称和图标之上。对于欧盟的应用，外部购买无需提供相应的IAP版本，而警告信息可能会让用户觉得外部支付不如苹果的支付系统安全或隐私。文章还提到，根据DMA（数字市场法），苹果不能在购买时设置“惊吓屏幕”。评论中，有人担心这种警告可能被用户视为质量标志，而其他人则批评苹果对开发者不友好，暗示其行为类似过去的微软。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果对iOS应用的订阅和支付政策，尤其是其警告信息和对开发者、用户的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持引入第三方服务以缓解订阅疲劳**：figassis认为像Setapp这样的服务可以帮助解决订阅疲劳和应用内广告问题，尤其是对儿童应用而言。这种模式可以避免依赖单独的订阅。

• **批评苹果的警告信息适得其反**：seydor指出苹果的警告信息不仅没有起到预期效果，反而可能让用户认为有警告的应用更便宜，从而选择这些应用。用户已经习惯于忽视警告信息。

• **反垄断和法律干预的必要性**：cadamsdotcom认为除非美国政府开始执行反垄断法，否则苹果不会停止其行为。欧盟的法律被认为是针对这些垄断行为的有效 backup 计划。

• **对苹果双重标准的质疑**：fundatus提到亚马逊应用没有收到这种警告，尽管它也只使用“外部购买”，质疑苹果是否在执行双重标准。

• **对苹果政策的不满和转向其他平台**：Fizzadar表示对苹果的用户和开发者不友好政策的不满，已经决定转向Android平台，并计划使用不含谷歌组件的设备。akmarinov则开玩笑说也许应该让Tim Cook卸任，让Schiller接管。

• **对苹果税收政策的失望**：akie认为苹果通过警告信息来施压那些不愿意支付30%苹果税的应用，这种做法令人失望但并不意外。

• **普遍认为对所有人都不利**：relistan认为这种情况对所有人都不利，但并不令人惊讶。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到苹果的警告信息可能被用户忽视或误解，从而产生反效果。
• 对苹果政策的双重标准和反垄断问题有多次提及，显示出用户对苹果垄断行为的强烈不满。
• 一些用户已经考虑转向其他平台，如Android或Linux，显示出对苹果生态系统的失望和流失可能性。

Critical Warning for External Purchases in App Store
Viktor Maric
:
first time seeing this. Apple will punish the apps with external payment system
Swift Dev
:
Yup it’s real, you see this warning if the app doesn’t use IAP.
Also it says external purchases next to the “get” button
It’s confusing to follow all the changes, but apparently—unlike
in the US
—external purchases
in the EU
don’t need to have corresponding IAP versions.
The warning adds five lines of text at the top of the App Store screen, above even the app’s name and icon.
On macOS, Apple declares three
levels of alerts
:
Informational (app icon): “to be used to inform the user about a current or impending event”
Warning (app icon): “to be used to warn the user about a current or impending event[…] when the alert’s content is more severe than [informational]”
Critical (orange ! triangle icon): “Use a caution symbol
sparingly
. Using a caution symbol like
exclamationmark.triangle
too frequently in your alerts diminishes its significance. Use the symbol only when extra attention is really needed, as when confirming an action that might result in unexpected loss of data.”
Guess which icon the App Store uses for external payments.
But I wonder how many users will see the warnings. If you’ve already purchased an app, it can auto-update to add external payments without your having to go back to the store. And I think the DMA mandated that there
can’t be scare screens
at the time of purchase.

data.title: EU ruling: tracking-based advertising [...] across Europe has no legal basis
data.author: mschuster91
data.article_summary: 比利时上诉法院裁定，“透明度与 consent 框架”（TCF）用于获取数据处理同意是违法的。TCF被谷歌、微软、亚马逊等公司在80%的互联网上使用。该裁决支持了比利时数据保护局的2022年裁定，指出TCF在实时竞价（RTB）系统中非法，该系统广泛用于跟踪用户行为并分享其数据。由于RTB缺乏安全性，无法告知用户数据如何被使用，也无法满足同意请求的必要条件。这一裁决在全欧洲立即生效，呼吁行业放弃基于跟踪的广告模式。此次判决被视为保护用户隐私的重要胜利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据隐私和广告跟踪的合法性、道德性及其对企业与消费者的影响

不同观点：
• sensanaty认为公司应极为谨慎地处理涉及个人身份信息（PII）的数据，甚至应对数据收集行为感到畏惧，并尽快删除不必要的数据。他批评企业过度收集数据，并支持通过法律手段限制这种行为。

• jqpabc123反对个性化广告，认为其不仅侵犯隐私，还对消费者和广告买家不利，提倡基于上下文的广告投放，认为这种方法更尊重隐私且更有效。

• morjom对未提供实际链接表示质疑，并提供了相关链接供进一步查阅，关注法律裁决的透明度和信息获取。

• lucianbr对新法规的即时适用性表示困惑，质疑其实际执行效果，并预测大型公司如Google不会轻易停止当前的广告模式。

• caseyy以讽刺的语气指出，虽然不希望有恶劣行为，但对未来的不良行为仍抱有好奇心，尤其关注“正当利益”概念的滥用。

43992444.article_content:
Landmark court decision against “TCF” consent pop ups on 80% of the internet
14 May 2025
(Updated on 15 May to include links to the judgement)
Google, Microsoft, Amazon, X, and the entire tracking-based advertising industry rely on the “Transparency & Consent Framework” (TCF) to obtain “consent” for data processing. This evening the Belgian Court of Appeal
ruled
that the TCF is illegal. The TCF is live on 80% of the Internet.
[1]
Today’s decision arises from enforcement by the Belgian Data Protection Authority, prompted by complainants coordinated by Dr
Johnny Ryan
, Director of
Enforce
at the Irish Council for Civil Liberties. The group of complainants are: Dr Johnny Ryan of Enforce, Katarzyna Szymielewicz of the
Panoptykon Foundation
,
Dr Jef Ausloos
,
Dr Pierre Dewitte
,
Stichting Bits of Freedom
, and
Ligue des Droits Humains
.
Dr Johnny Ryan said
"Today's court's decision shows that the consent system used by Google, Amazon, X, Microsoft, deceives hundreds of millions of Europeans. The tech industry has sought to hide its vast data breach behind sham consent popups. Tech companies turned the GDPR into a daily nuisance rather than a shield for people."
This Belgian enforcement arises from a chain of complaints and litigation across Europe initiated by Dr Ryan in 2018 against Real-Time Bidding (RTB).
Today’s decision confirmed the Belgian Data Protection Authority's 2022
finding of multiple infringements
by the TCF, closely echoing the complainants' submissions.
For seven years, the tracking industry has used the TCF as a legal cover for Real-Time Bidding (RTB), the vast advertising auction system that operates behind the scenes on websites and apps. RTB tracks what Internet users look at and where they go in the real world. It then continuously broadcasts this data to a host of companies, enabling them to keep dossiers on every Internet user.
[2]
Because there is no security in the RTB system it is impossible to know what then happens to the data. As a result, it is also impossible to provide the necessary information that must accompany a consent request.
[3]
Today’s judgement confirms the Belgian Data Protection Authority’s 2022 decision. It applies immediately across Europe.
Dr Ryan of Enforce said “
This decision is momentous. It creates a clear need for industry to innovate and move away from the dangerous, ineffective, and fraud-riddled tracking-based advertising. RTB can operate without personal data. This decision shows that it must. This good news for every person online, and for publishers, too.
”
We thank our lawyers
Frederic Debusseré
and
Ruben Roex
, of
Timelex
.
Links
See chronology, evidence, and explainers about RTB
https://www.iccl.ie/RTB/
Brussels Appeals Court judgement (Dutch original)
https://www.iccl.ie/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Arrest-Marktenhof-14-05-2025.pdf
Brussels Appeals Court judgement (MACHINE TRANSLATION to English)
https://www.iccl.ie/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Arrest-Marktenhof-14-05-2025-en.pdf
Notes
[1]
See "IAB & IAB Tech Lab Respond with Support for OpenRTB and IAB Europe’s Transparency & Consent Framework", October 19 2020
https://iabtechlab.com/iab-and-tech-lab-respond-with-support-for-open-rtb-and-iab-europes-transparency-consent-framework/
[2]
For detail on the scale of RTB see our report "The Biggest Data Breach: ICCL report on the scale of Real-Time Bidding data broadcasts in the U.S. and Europe", ICCL, May 2022
https://www.iccl.ie/digital-data/iccl-report-on-the-scale-of-real-time-bidding-data-broadcasts-in-the-u-s-and-europe/
[3]
"
As it is technically impossible for the user to have prior information about every data controller involved in a real-time bidding (RTB) scenario, programmatic trading, the area of fastest growth in digital advertising spend, would seem, at least prima facie, to be incompatible with consent under GDPR
". See
e-mail
and page 3 of
attached lobbying paper
from IAB Europe CEO Townsend Feehan to European Commission, 26 June 2017, obtained by Enforce using Freedom of Information.
43992444.article_summary: 比利时上诉法院裁定，“透明度与 consent 框架”（TCF）用于获取数据处理同意是违法的。TCF被谷歌、微软、亚马逊等公司在80%的互联网上使用。该裁决支持了比利时数据保护局的2022年裁定，指出TCF在实时竞价（RTB）系统中非法，该系统广泛用于跟踪用户行为并分享其数据。由于RTB缺乏安全性，无法告知用户数据如何被使用，也无法满足同意请求的必要条件。这一裁决在全欧洲立即生效，呼吁行业放弃基于跟踪的广告模式。此次判决被视为保护用户隐私的重要胜利。

data.title: Bitwarden registration flow failed – so I wrote a stand-up comedy set instead
data.author: Yulenka
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Bitwarden应用注册流程中的一个逻辑缺陷，由一位自称“Юленька”的人以严肃、讽刺和单口相声的方式记录。用户在设备A上启动注册，但最终在设备B上完成，包括设置主密码。这导致两个设备的账户创建失败，应用无法使用。问题的核心在于未验证的设备会话连续性。提交问题后，Bitwarden的客服回复不够具体，引发了一段讽刺性的单口相声式描述。文章最后提到，虽然Bitwarden后来表示无法重现问题，但作者怀疑问题可能已在更新中默默修复。作者呼吁改善UX设计，避免类似问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bitwarden注册流程的用户体验问题以及用户对不良UX的反馈方式

不同观点：
• Yulenka认为Bitwarden的注册流程存在问题，导致其无法顺利完成注册。她没有选择直接提交bug报告，而是通过一种幽默、喜剧化的方式，在GitHub上发布了一个带有 markdown、截图和调侃性质的“表演”来表达她的挫折感。她强调用户体验（UX）是安全的一部分，间接批评了软件在UX设计上的不足。

• 另一种隐含的观点是，用户在遇到不良UX时可能会采取创造性的方式表达不满，而不是直接反馈给开发者。Yulenka的幽默和“表演”不仅是她个人的发泄方式，也可能代表了一部分用户在遇到类似问题时的无力感和选择通过非传统方式表达反馈的倾向。

补充讨论：
• Yulenka特别提到，她的反馈中没有恶意，只是通过幽默和一些技术工具（如markdown和截图）来展示她的经历。这表明她希望通过一种轻松的方式引起开发者对问题的关注，而不是正式投诉。

• 争议的焦点可能在于，开发者是否会认真对待这种非传统的反馈方式。虽然Yulenka的反馈充满创意且无恶意，但它是否能有效促成问题的解决仍是一个问题。这反映了在软件开发和用户反馈过程中，用户体验问题反馈形式的有效性和开发者接受度之间的潜在矛盾。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，Yulenka提到“UX是安全的一部分”，这指出了UX设计不仅仅关乎用户的便利性，还直接影响到用户在使用软件时的整体安全性。如果注册流程出现问题，可能导致用户无法安全地使用软件，从而影响整体的安全体验。

bitwarden-registration-theatre
A logical flaw in Bitwarden’s registration flow, documented with seriousness, sarcasm and stand-up.
🧠 What happened
This repository exists to document a flaw in the registration process of the Bitwarden app — discovered and dissected by someone who happens to think like a security architect but signs off as "Юленька".
It’s a classic case of a security-focused UX that gets everything right — until it doesn't.
🕳️ The Logical Flaw
Downloaded the Bitwarden app on
Device A
(iPad).
Entered email, pressed Register.
The app said:
"Check your inbox to continue registration."
Opened the email
on Device B
(iPhone), clicked the link.
Was allowed to continue registration on Device B, including setting the master password.
After submission, the flow failed. Account creation broken. Both apps unusable.
❓ Why this matters
The user is allowed to
initiate
registration on Device A.
But
finalize
it on Device B — including defining the
master password
, the key to everything.
Once the second device submits the data, Bitwarden collapses into a broken state.
If you're building a security-first product, don’t rely on unverified device-session continuity. Period.
📬 The Support Response
After reporting the issue with precision, clarity, and civility… the response was:
"Thanks for your message. Please check our help center."
Which — while expected — also gave birth to...
🎤 The Stand-Up Sketch
English version:
standup.md
Russian original:
sketch.md
Because if they won’t answer you seriously, you might as well answer them artistically.
🧾 License
This repository is public domain. Steal the story, fix the UX. Just don’t build another Schrödinger flow.
Sincerely,
Юленька
🕵️ Post Scriptum
After sending my report, Bitwarden replied and mentioned that they couldn’t reproduce the issue.
Fair enough.
However, I wrote to them weeks ago — and it’s possible the issue was silently patched in the meantime.
No changelog, no confession. Just mysterious UX justice.
I’m not saying
my Markdown theatre changed anything.
But I’m also not
not
saying that.

data.title: Moving Forth: a series on writing Forth kernels
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文列出了Bradford J. Rodriguez发表的各类论文、研讨会、计算机程序，涵盖Forth内核设计、多任务处理、多处理器系统、专家控制系统等主题。主要系列包括《Moving Forth》系列，详细讲解Forth内核设计及其实现；多篇关于多任务和多处理器系统的文章，如《Multiprocessing for the Impoverished》系列；以及1997年博士论文《An Embedded Temporal Expert For Control of a Tandem Accelerator》和1989年硕士论文《PatternForth: A Pattern-Matching Language for Real-Time Control》。此外，还包括关于Forth汇编器、模式匹配语言、MIDI控制器等主题的杂文和计算机程序代码，如CamelForth在不同处理器上的实现。所有内容均附带文本、图片及相关链接，部分为PDF格式。
data.comments_summary:

补充讨论：
• 评论提到了一个具体的文化参考，即《Starting FORTH》这本书，这表明该系列标题可能具有历史和技术背景，对理解整个系列的内容可能有帮助。
• 评论者通过提供在线阅读链接，暗示读者可以通过查阅该书来加深对系列内容的理解，表明这本书可能与系列主题密切相关。
• 没有其他观点或争议提出，评论主要是在分享信息和提供资源。

data.title: 89M Steam accounts reportedly leaked. Change your password now
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 约8900万Steam用户账号信息 reportedly 被黑客窃取，具体 breach 方式不明。网络安全公司 Underdark 披露，一名黑客在暗网论坛上以5000美元出售这些数据。尽管最初怀疑是第三方供应商 Trillio 的问题，但 Steam 母公司 Valve 确认并未使用 Trillio。目前细节仍不明确，建议用户更改密码、启用双因素认证（2FA）、检查邮箱可疑活动，并警惕钓鱼诈骗。调查仍在进行中。

43992371.article_content:
Stay vigilant, Steam users.
Credit: Jakub Porzycki / NurPhoto / Getty Images
The account details of 89 million Steam users have reportedly been hacked.
Although how the breach happened is unclear, this is a good time to change your password and enable
two-factor authentication
.
The past Sunday, cybersecurity firm
Underdark
posted on LinkedIn about a data breach. That post was then picked up and widely spread by gaming-focused
X user
Mellow_Online1, as reported by tech outlet
XDA
. According to Underdark's post, "a threat actor going by Machine1337 posted on a well-known dark web forum claiming to have breached Steam, offering a dataset of over 89 million user records for $5,000."

This claim from Machine1337 reportedly also included a Telegram contact, a link to sample data, and internal vendor data "indicating deeper access."
The breach was believed to have come from a third party service, not directly from Steam. Initially, Mellow_Online1 thought it was from a vendor called Trillio. But Valve, Steam's parent company, confirmed to Mellow_Online1 that it doesn't use Trillio.
Details are hazy at this point. Mashable has reached out to Valve for confirmation and specifics of how the breach occurred and will update this story if we receive a response. In the meantime, Steam users are advised to change their password, turn on 2FA, check their email for any suspicious activity, and be extra vigilant about phishing scams that seem to be related to Steam.

data.title: Appeals court rules that tracking-based online advertising is illegal in Europe
data.author: adwmayer
data.article_summary: 比利时上诉法院裁定，目前用于大多数在线广告的透明度和同意框架（TCF）在欧盟是非法的。该决定支持了比利时数据保护局2022年的调查结果，即支撑在线广告的技术违反了欧盟《通用数据保护条例》（GDPR）的多项原则。TCF由互动广告局创建，旨在标准化网站请求用户同意被追踪的方式，但被认定在GDPR下非法。隐私倡导者认为，谷歌、亚马逊、微软等公司通过虚假同意弹窗欺骗了数亿欧洲人。尽管互动广告局对判决表示部分宽慰，但仍需根据裁定调整其广告技术框架，未来监管机构将监督其修改。

43992337.article_content:
Read full article
anna washenko
Contributing Reporter
Wed, May 14, 2025, 6:37 PM
·
2 min read
0
Reuters / Reuters
The Belgian Court of Appeal
ruled today
that the Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF) currently used as the foundation for most online advertising is illegal in the EU. This decision upholds the findings of the Belgian Data Protection Authority
from 2022
that the technology underpinning online ads violates several principles of the
General Data Protection Regulations
, an EU digital privacy law that took effect in 2018.
Engadget's Daniel Cooper wrote a thorough
explainer
of the different systems that support the current online advertising ecosystem, which is valuable reading for anybody spending time online. The very simplified version is that advertisers participate in real-time bidding (RTB) to show their content online. Currently, those bids are based on information gathered from tracking individuals' activities online with cookies. The TCF was created by the Interactive Advertising Bureau as a way to standardize how websites ask users for permission to be tracked. The original 2022 decision determined that both the consent collected by the TCF and the data collected in the RTB process were illegal under the GDPR.
"Today's court's decision shows that the consent system used by Google, Amazon, X,
Microsoft
, deceives hundreds of millions of Europeans,"
said
Dr Johnny Ryan, director of Enforce at the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, who has been leading the legal charge against the current approach to ad tech. "The tech industry has sought to hide its vast data breach behind sham consent popups. Tech companies turned the GDPR into a daily nuisance rather than a shield for people."
ADVERTISEMENT
Advertisement
The
reaction
from IAB Europe, which filed the appeal, seems to mostly be relief that it hasn't been found responsible for the data collected by TCF. "The Market Court has rejected the APD’s view that IAB Europe is a joint controller together with TCF participants for their own respective processing of personal data, for instance for the purpose of digital advertising," the organization's statement says. IAB Europe notes that it has already suggested changes to the TCF that better reflect the "limited controllership" and submitted them to the Belgian Data Protection Authority. The group faced fines and was ordered to rebuild its current ad-tech framework as a result of the original decision.
We've also reached out to some of the major advertisers that use the RTB technology for comment on the ruling.
While this does seem like a big win for privacy advocates and internet users in the EU, it's unclear exactly what the next steps will be for advertisers and for ad tech systems. Most likely, regulators will oversee changes the IAB Europe makes to the TCF, so consent pop-ups may not yet be a thing of the past.

data.title: Bus stops here: Shanghai lets riders design their own routes
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 上海推出了一种新的众包公交平台，允许乘客设计、投票并激活新公交线路，最快三天内即可开通。该系统名为“定制公交”（DZ），居民可通过平台提交建议路线，若需求达到门槛（通常每次行程15至20人），路线即可开通。目前，全市已开通超过220条DZ线路。乘客需在线输入起点、终点、时间及频率，若获批，路线可在三天内运行。首个试点DZ301路线连接地铁站与住宅区、学校和办公楼，日均客流250至260人。专家表示，该系统能更好匹配运力与需求，提升便利性和资源利用率。尽管目前票价无特殊优惠，但新平台缩短了传统繁琐的线路审批过程，仍需提升规划和宣传。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公共交通系统的创新与优化，特别是基于需求的自优化交通方案

不同观点：
• **支持自优化交通方案**：
   - jillesvangurp：认为这是一种聪明的低技术解决方案，可以根据需求自优化，并与Uber类比，强调只要时间可预测且合理，乘客会满意。
   - ketzo：赞赏该概念，认为公共空间设计可以通过群众的智慧进行改进，尤其在中国/上海这样高密度和强执行力的地方可能实现。
   - philberto：提到德国汉堡的Moia服务，已经实现了虚拟站点，根据乘客需求调整路线。
   - dluan：以上海为例，说明其公交系统的现代化和便捷性，例如显示下一班车距离的LCD屏幕。

• **质疑与挑战**：
   - liampulles：提到南非的“出租车”系统，虽然是一种自底向上的解决方案，但存在暴力卡特尔问题，并非完全正面。
   - zaptheimpaler：认为中国有能力快速实施此类项目，而西方社会因繁文缛节而受阻，项目推进缓慢。
   - originalvichy：提到赫尔辛基曾尝试类似项目但因需求低而关闭，现有公交系统已经最大化利用了人口密度。
   - nitwit005：担心用户参与度低，导致系统无法有效运作。

• **其他变体与算法**：
   - charlieyu1：提到香港的小巴系统，司机根据乘客需求调整停站，有时 entire areas 会被跳过。
   - comrade1234：瑞士的火车/公交服务每年根据使用数据调整，但可能被操纵。
   - parpfish：提出让人们设计自己的政治区划以减少选区划分不公，但担心复杂性和算法选择带来的政治影响。

• **对基础设施的批评**：
   - kr2：来自洛杉矶，羡慕中国、丹麦、日本和瑞士的公共交通系统，批评美国基础设施的糟糕状态。

• **技术与数据**：
   - boatsie：建议谷歌可以利用人们的日常通勤数据推荐公交路线和时间，尽管存在隐私问题。

补充讨论：
• **公民参与的复杂性**：
   - altilunium：指出有些公民不愿意参与复杂的投票过程，只希望获得快速服务，这取决于多数人的公民参与意识。

争议焦点：
• 自优化交通方案的可行性与可持续性，特别是在不同文化和政治背景下的实施挑战。
• 公民参与和技术数据在优化公共交通中的作用与潜在问题。

43980845.article_content:
NEWS
Bus Stops Here: Shanghai Lets Riders Design Their Own Routes
A new crowd-sourced transit platform allows riders to propose, vote on, and activate new bus lines in as little as three days.
By
Chen Yiru
May 09, 2025
#
transport
#
urban planning
From early-morning school drop-offs to seniors booking rides to the hospital, from suburban commuters seeking a faster link to the metro to families visiting ancestral graves, Shanghai is rolling out a new kind of public bus — one that’s designed by commuters, and launched only when enough riders request it.
Branded “DZ” for
dingzhi
, or “customized,” the system invites residents to submit proposed routes through a city-run platform. Others with similar travel needs can opt in or vote, and if demand meets the threshold — typically 15 to 20 passengers per trip — the route goes live.
More than 220 DZ routes have already launched across all 16 city districts. Through an online platform opened May 8, users enter start and end points, preferred times, and trip frequency. If approved, routes can begin running in as little as three days.
One of the first test cases was DZ301, a pilot route linking a major metro station with surrounding residential blocks, schools, and office buildings. “The average daily passenger flow is 250 to 260 people — 170 to 180 during the morning peak and 70 to 80 in the evening,” Wu Yongming, deputy manager at Jiushi Bus Company,
told
domestic media.
The route originated from a resident’s request submitted last December. In response, transit staff conducted on-site research, observing foot traffic, speaking with commuters, and calculating turnover times during peak hours. Drivers then ran trial runs to fine-tune the schedule before the route officially launched.
Chen Xiaohong, a professor at Tongji University’s School of Transportation, said the system builds on Shanghai’s dense transit network to better match capacity with demand, improving both convenience and resource use during peak travel.
Proposed routes appear on a “Popular Customization” page, where others can opt in to help reach the launch threshold. Group bookings can also fast-track approval. Fares are market-based, and while they follow basic public transit standards, no discounts are currently offered for students, seniors, or other groups.
Wang Yixiang, deputy director of the city’s Passenger Transport Department,
said
the new platform shortens what was once a slow, bureaucratic process for launching new routes. But he acknowledged early challenges: passenger demand is uneven, public awareness remains low, and planning still relies heavily on manual fieldwork.
“Going forward, we need to improve route planning, upgrade platform functions, and boost visibility,” Wang said.
(Header image: A “DZ” bus arrives at a residential area in Shanghai, 2025. From Weibo)

data.title: EM-LLM: Human-Inspired Episodic Memory for Infinite Context LLMs
data.author: jbotz
data.article_summary: EM-LLM是一种受人类情景记忆启发的大语言模型，能够在无需微调的情况下处理几乎无限长度的上下文。该模型通过结合贝叶斯 surprise 和图论边界优化，将输入序列组织成连贯的情景事件，并采用基于相似性和时间连续性的双阶段记忆检索机制，实现高效的信息访问。实验表明，EM-LLM在LongBench和∞-Bench基准测试中优于现有的SOTA模型InfLLM，并在多种任务中超越了RAG模型，同时在10M tokens规模的检索任务中表现出色。该模型的事件分割与人类感知事件高度相关，为探索人类记忆机制提供了一个新的计算框架。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Transformer模型中的记忆机制与注意力机制优化

不同观点：
• **killerstorm** 认为这种方法通过在单个token序列内运作，与“情节记忆”隐喻相吻合，但与人们通常对“记忆”的期望不同。它将transformer的注意力分为粗粒度（k-NN算法选择token范围）和细粒度（常规注意力机制）两部分，适用于长上下文情境，但在需要考虑大量不同事实时效率不高。

• **mountainriver** 提出压缩信息进入潜在空间是解决计算不可行性的更强方法，暗示TTT、cannon layers和titans等方法可能更有效。

• **p_v_doom** 表示对情节记忆模型的兴趣，认为其对神经网络很有用，并乐见人们进行相关测试。

• **MacsHeadroom** 关注该方法是否会导致计算时间增加，并比较其与RAG（检索增强生成）方法的适用场景。

补充讨论：
- **killerstorm** 强调了该方法在处理长上下文时的优势以及在大量事实检索中的不足。
- **mountainriver** 指出了计算复杂性问题，并提出了信息压缩的替代方案。
- **p_v_doom** 从历史角度讨论了情节记忆模型在神经网络中的潜在价值。
- **MacsHeadroom** 提出了对该方法运行效率和应用场景的实际考虑。

EM-LLM: Human-inspired Episodic Memory for Infinite Context LLMs
This repository contains a version of the code for EM-LLM, published in
ICLR 2025
:
[openreview link]
.
Quick Links
Overview
Usage
Citation
Overview
While typical LLMs struggle with processing extensive contexts, the human brain excels at organising and retrieving experiences spanning a lifetime. In this work, we introduce EM-LLM, an architecture that integrates key aspects of human episodic memory and event cognition into LLMs with
no fine-tuning
, enabling them to handle practically infinite context lengths while maintaining computational efficiency. EM-LLM organises sequences of tokens into coherent episodic events using a combination of Bayesian surprise and graph-theoretic boundary refinement in an online fashion. When needed, these events are retrieved through a two-stage memory process, combining similarity-based and temporally contiguous retrieval for efficient and human-like access to relevant information. Experiments on the LongBench and
$\infty$
-Bench benchmarks demonstrate EM-LLM's superior performance, consistently outperforming the SOTA retrieval model InfLLM across various baseline LLMs. In addition, EM-LLM
outperforms RAG
in a wide range of tasks, while requiring similar resources. Notably, EM-LLM's performance even
surpasses full-context models
in most tasks, while successfully performing retrieval across
10M tokens
- a scale computationally infeasible for such models. Our analysis reveals strong correlations between EM-LLM's event segmentation and human-perceived events, suggesting a bridge between this artificial system and its biological counterpart, thereby offering a novel computational framework for exploring human memory mechanisms.
Architecture
Figure 1:
Architecture of memory formation and retrieval in each LLM layer.
Formation:
Input sequence is initially segmented via surprise (purple dashed lines in ①), then segmentation is refined based on group theoretic metrics (green dashed lines in ②). Initial tokens and local context are preserved.
Retrieval:
via both k-NN search ③ and selecting contiguous events from episodic memory ④.
Results
Click
here
more complete result tables.
Figure 2:
(Left)
EM-LLM$_S$ vs. RAG (NV-Embed-v2 retriever) vs. full-context, with LLaMA-3.1-8B as the base LLM, evaluated on LongBench.
(Right)
Comparison of various long-sequence methods (sorted based on their context window length) on an extended version of
$\infty$
-Bench's
Retrieve.PassKey
.
Usage
Configuration
Install requirements:
python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r "${base_dir}/requirements.txt"
pip install -e "${base_dir}/."
The YAML files used for configuration can be found in the
config/
directory.

data.title: It Awaits Your Experiments
data.author: pavel_lishin
data.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了诗人Christian Bök的《Xenotext实验》，这是一个将诗歌编码到细菌DNA中的艺术项目。Bök试图创作世界上第一个能生物自我复制的诗歌，通过将一段对话编码到微生物的基因中，使其产生相应的蛋白质作为回应。该项目选择以耐极端环境的**Deinococcus radiodurans**细菌为目标，但由于初期技术不足，Bök自学了遗传学、蛋白质组学和编码等相关技能，并与科学家团队合作攻克技术难关。虽然初期在**E. coli**实验中遇到编码混乱问题，但项目最终取得进展。文章还讨论了艺术与科学关系的转变，指出在该项目中，科学开始为艺术服务，改变了传统的艺术与科学主从关系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Peter Watts的科幻作品《Blindsight》及相关科学概念，Christian Bök的Xenotext项目，以及对特定细菌Deinococcus radiodurans的讨论。

不同观点：
• jkingsman高度评价Peter Watts的《Blindsight》，认为它是极硬的科幻作品，充满丰富的概念，并与其他作品如Charles Stross的《Accelerando》进行比较，认为Watts的作品虽然概念密集但不如《Accelerando》那样自娱自乐。
• Atreiden对Bök的Xenotext项目表示极大兴趣，认为其设想宏大，并对其艺术不朽的理念感到震撼，表示有意阅读Bök的小说。
• dejobaan将Bök的项目与Tom7的项目进行比较，认为虽然不及Bök的水平，但这类实验性项目提醒人们可以进行有趣且创新的工作。
• davidthewatson提供关于Bök在多伦多活动的信息，并幽默地希望这不会成为意外的超级热门事件。
• MinimalAction对Bök的作品产生浓厚兴趣，并通过阅读了解了耐辐射细菌Deinococcus radiodurans，以及其与panspermia理论的联系。
• alnwlsn对文章中提到的“唯一在月球上生存的生物”表示疑问，并提到Surveyor 3相机事件中争议的Streptococcus mitis。
• dekhn作为相关领域的博士，表示对文章中的技术细节不太理解，特别是蛋白质序列映射到文本以及其功能和加密诗歌的能力。
• sriram_malhar对Bök的Xenotext项目表示惊叹，对其创意和持久努力表示赞赏。
• flobosg长期关注Bök的工作，对其持续的创新表示赞赏，并分享了Ulver对Bök诗歌的音乐演绎。
• flysand7将Bök的项目与Yakushimaru Etsuko的“I'm Humanity”项目进行比较，并分享了相关链接。
• SideburnsOfDoom指出文章中对Deinococcus radiodurans需氧性的描述与维基百科上的信息有出入，请求澄清。
• aaroninsf对Peter Watts的《Rifters》系列提出严厉批评，认为其包含未编辑的性暴力幻想，不值得推荐。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Peter Watts作品中涉及的性暴力内容，aaroninsf认为这些内容使其作品不值得推荐，而其他评论者如jkingsman则关注其科幻概念的创新性。
• 对Deinococcus radiodurans的生物特性存在疑问，特别是其需氧性与文章描述之间的矛盾，引发对科学准确性的讨论。
• 对Christian Bök的Xenotext项目的兴趣和赞赏是评论中的一个主要正面主题，许多人对其创意和艺术不朽的理念表示钦佩。

43974005.article_content:
No Moods, Ads or Cutesy Fucking Icons
In love with the moment. Scared shitless of the future.
«
A Synopsis of Squid
12
May
2025
It Awaits Your Experiments.
You may have heard of Christian Bök. You
may
have
read
about
him
on this very blog if you’ve been hanging out here long enough. Perhaps you were even one of the very select few to witness the seminal talk I gave back in 2016
[1]
—“ScArt: or, How to Tell When You’ve Finished Fucking”— which climaxed with a glowing description of Bök’s magnum opus, then still in progress. And if you read
Echopraxia
, you’ll have encountered—without even knowing it— a brief cameo of that work near the end, suggesting that at least in the Blindopraxia timeline, he’d brought his baby to fruition.
Truth to tell, I didn’t know if he was actually going to pull it off for the longest time. I thought he’d given up years ago.
Yes. This is excerpted from a book of
poetry.
All of these pictures are.
The story so far: back in the early two-thousands Christian Bök, famous for accomplishments lesser poets would never even dream of attempting (he once wrote
a book
in which each chapter contained only a single vowel) started work on the world’s first biologically-self-replicating poem: the
Xenotext Experiment
, which aspired to encode a poem into the genetic code of a bacterium. Not just a poem, either: a
dialog
. The DNA encoding one half of that exchange (“Orpheus” by name) was designed to function both as text and as a functional gene. The protein it coded for functioned as the other half (“Eurydice”), a sort of call-and-response between the gene and its product. The protein was also designed to fluoresce red, which might seem a tad gratuitous until you realize that “Eurydice”’s half of the dialog contains the phrase “the faery is rosy/of glow”.
Phase One involved engineering Orpheus and Eurydice into the benign and ubiquitous
E. coli
, just to work out the bugs. Ultimately, though, the target microbe was
Deinococcus radiodurans
: also known as “Conan the Bacterium” on account of being one of the toughest microbial motherfuckers on the planet. To quote Bök himself:
Astronauts fear it. Biologists fear it. It is not human. It lives in isolation. It grows in complete darkness. It derives no energy from the Sun. It feeds on asbestos. It feeds on concrete. It inhabits a gold seam on level 104 of the Mponeng Mine in Johannesburg. It lives in alkaline lakelets full of arsenic. It grows in lagoons of boiling asphalt. It thrives in a deadly miasma of hydrogen sulphide. It breathes iron. It breathes rust. It needs no oxygen to live. It can survive for a decade without water. It can withstand temperatures of 323 k, hot enough to melt rubidium. It can sleep for 100 millennia inside a crystal of salt, buried in Death Valley. It does not die in the hellish infernos at the Städtbibliothek during the ﬁrebombing of Dresden. It does not burn when exposed to ultraviolet rays. It does not reproduce via the use of dna. It breeds, unseen, inside canisters of hairspray. It feeds on polyethylene. It feeds on hydrocarbons. It inhabits caustic geysers of steam near the Grand Prismatic Spring in Yellowstone National Park.
I’d love to quote all seven glorious and terrifying pages, but to keep within the bounds of Fair Use I’ll skip ahead to the end:
It is totally inhuman. It does not love you. It does not need you. It does not even know that you exist. It is invincible. It is unkillable. It has lived through five mass extinctions. It is the only known organism to have ever lived on the Moon. It awaits your experiments.
As things turned out, it had to await somewhat longer than expected. The project hinged upon molecular techniques that did not exist when the experiment began. Christian taught himself the relevant skills— genetics, proteomics, coding— and enlisted a team of scientists (not to mention a supercomputer or two) to invent them. It was fine when Art came to science in search of inspiration; that’s as it should be. I suppose it was okay— if a little iffy— when Science started going back to Art for solutions to scientific and technical problems. But this crosses a line: with
The Xenotext

data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何缓解学习Rust过程中的困难，提出了几个重要建议以帮助学习者节省时间和减少挫败感。首先，学习者需要放下成见，接受Rust独特的思维模式，包括生命周期、所有权和trait系统等新概念。应将编译器视为合作者而非对手，通过编译器的提示来理解代码问题。Rust的冗长代码实际上有助于构建大型应用，提供更多上下文和支持重构。学习者应从小步骤开始，初期多使用简单方法和工具，逐步引入复杂概念，并善用Rust playground进行实验。文章还强调了准确性和持续练习的重要性，通过不断编写代码来提高阅读和理解Rust的能力。最后，建议打开所有Clippy提示以遵循最佳实践。

• ants_everywhere指出学习曲线的存在意味着学习过程中会有进步，但也暗示Rust的学习曲线可能过于陡峭。
• doug_durham认为Rust的复杂性反映了其人体工程学问题，需要平衡所获得的功能和所付出的努力。
• the__alchemist分享了自己在Rust编程中避开一些复杂特性的经验，并提出了对使用更抽象特性（如Cow）的疑问。

补充讨论：
• Rust的所有权和借用机制是讨论的核心，支持者认为这些机制有助于编写更安全的代码，批评者则认为其复杂且难以理解。
• Rust的语法和宏的使用也被视为学习的一大障碍，尤其是对那些没有系统编程背景的程序员。
• 不同背景的程序员对Rust的接受程度不同，有系统编程经验的人通常更容易上手。
• 对于Rust是否能成为主流的系统编程语言，存在不同看法，一些人认为其潜力巨大，另一些人则持怀疑态度。

争议焦点：
• Rust的语法复杂性和不直观的特性是主要争议点，尤其是对新手和非系统编程背景的程序员来说。
• 借用检查器和所有权模型的严格性被认为是Rust的一大特色，但也有人认为这些机制增加了学习难度。

Rust Insights
Flattening Rust's Learning Curve
Published: 2025-05-05
I see people make the same mistakes over and over again when learning Rust.
Here are my thoughts (ordered by importance) on how you can ease the learning process.
My goal is to help you save time and frustration.
Let Your Guard Down
Stop resisting. That’s the most important lesson.
Accept that learning Rust requires adopting a completely different mental model than what you’re used to.
There are a ton of new concepts to learn like lifetimes, ownership, and the trait system.
And depending on your background, you’ll need to add generics, pattern matching, or macros to the list.
Your learning pace doesn’t have much to do with whether you’re smart or not or if you have a lot of programming experience.
Instead, what matters more is
your attitude toward the language
.
I have seen junior devs excel at Rust with no prior training and senior engineers struggle for weeks/months or even give up entirely. Leave your hubris at home.
Treat the borrow checker as a co-author, not an adversary. This reframes the relationship.
Let the compiler do the teaching: for example, this works great with lifetimes, because the compiler will tell you when a lifetime is ambiguous.
Then just add it but take the time to reason about
why
the compiler couldn’t figure it out itself.

longest
(
x
:
&
str
,
y
:
&
str
)
->
&
str
{
if
x
.
len
(
)
>
y
.
len
(
)
{
x
}
else
{
y
}
}
If you try to compile this, the compiler will ask you to add a lifetime parameter.
It provides this helpful suggestion:
1
|
fn
longest
<
'a
>
(
x
:
&
'a
str
,
y
:
&
'a
str
)
->

{
|
+

So you don’t have to guess what the compiler wants and can follow its instructions.
But also sit down and wonder
why
the compiler couldn’t figure it out itself.
Most of the time when fighting the compiler it is actually exposing a design flaw.
Similarly, if your code gets overly verbose or looks ugly, there’s probably a better way.
Declare defeat and learn to do it the Rust way.
If you come from a dynamic language like Python, you’ll find that Rust is more verbose in general.
Most of it just comes from type annotations, though.
Some people might dismiss Rust as being “unelegant” or “ugly”, but the verbosity actually serves a good purpose and is immensely helpful for building large-scale applications:
First off, you will read the code more often than you write it,
which means type annotations will give you more local context to reason with.
Second, it helps immensely with refactoring because the compiler can check if you broke any code while you move things around.
If your code turns out to look very ugly, take a step back and ask if there’s a simpler solution.
Don’t dismiss the language right away.
Turn on all
clippy lints
on day one – even the pedantic ones.
Run the linter and follow the suggestions religiously.
Don’t skip that step once your program compiles.
Resistance is futile.
The longer you refuse to learn, the longer you will suffer;
but the moment you let your guard down is the moment you’ll start to learn.
Forget what you think you knew about programming and really start to listen to what the compiler, the standard library, and clippy are trying to tell you.
Baby Steps
I certainly tried to run before I could walk.
That alone cost me a lot of precious time.
Don’t make it too hard on yourself in the beginning.
Here are some tips:
Use
String
and
clone()
and
unwrap
generously; you can always refactor later – and refactoring is the best part about Rust!
I wrote an article on saving yourself time during that phase
here
.
Use simple if or match statements before starting to learn some of the more idiomatic
.and_then
etc. combinators
Avoid async Rust in week 1. The additional rules are a tax on people still learning the core ownership model.
Don’t introduce too many new concepts at the same time!
Instead, while you learn about a new concept, have an editor open and write out a few examples.
What helped was to just write some code in the
Rust playground
and try to get it to compile. Write super small snippets (e.g., one
main.rs
for one concept) instead of using one big “tutorial” repo.
Get into the habit of throwing most of your code away.
I still do that and test out ideas in the playground or when I brainstorm with clients.
For instance, here’s one of my favorite code snippets to explain the concept of ownership:
fn
my_func
(
v
:
String
)
{
//
do something with v
}
fn
main
(
)
{
let
s
=
String
::
from
(
"
hello
"
)
;
my_func
(
s
)
;
my_func
(
s
)
;
//
error, but why?
}
Can you fix it?
Can you explain it?
Ask yourself what would change if
v
was an
i32
.
If Rust code looks scary to you,
break it down
.
Write your own, simpler version, then slowly increase the complexity.
Rust is easier to write than to read.
By writing lots of Rust, you will also learn how to read it better as well.
Be Accurate
How you do anything is how you do everything.
– An ancient Rust proverb

data.title: Show HN: Airweave – Let agents search any app
data.author: lennertjansen
data.article_summary: Airweave 是一个工具，允许代理对任何应用程序进行语义搜索。它兼容 MCP，可无缝连接应用程序、数据库或 API，将内容转化为代理可用的知识。支持从 25+ 数据源同步，具备实体提取、增量更新、语义搜索等功能，并提供 Python 和 TypeScript/JavaScript SDK。技术栈包括 React/TypeScript 前端、FastAPI 后端、PostgreSQL 和 Qdrant 数据库，通过 Docker Compose 或 Kubernetes 部署。未来计划增加更多集成和 Kubernetes 支持。项目遵循 MIT 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Airweave产品及其MCP（Multi-Connector Protocol）服务器的可行性、技术细节、竞争优势及潜在挑战的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对连接器业务的警示**：[swyx] 提出警告，认为连接器业务非常艰难，历史上有许多失败案例。尽管有一些成功案例，如FiveTran，但背后的痛苦和失败很多。建议深入研究行业，避免重蹈覆辙。

• **关于LLM与数据存储交互的疑问**：[smattiso] 关心LLM如何更好地与底层数据存储交互，而不仅仅是通过简单的API搜索功能。建议通过预计算API结构，让LLM更有效地推理数据。

• **集成与同步的细节**：[throwaway314155] 询问集成是通过MCP实现还是传统方式，关注一次性/事件同步的支持情况，以及如何处理不同集成提供商之间的差异和数据同步问题。

• **界面选择的质疑**：[valianter] 质疑聊天界面是否是所有应用的最佳选择，认为搜索可能更自然。对MCP版本的Glean/Onyx等产品是否真正提升了用户体验表示不确定。

• **产品架构与盈利模式的疑问**：[beecasthurlbow] 关心代码库的完整性及与后端连接方式，同时询问Airweave的盈利模式和数据存储位置。

• **对产品的高度评价**：[reneBond] 对Airweave的检索准确性给予高度评价，认为其在第三方集成方面表现出色，并赞扬团队的支持服务。

• **对内部数据源集成的关注**：[ayxliu] 关心是否能集成公司内部的数据源。

• **对自托管数据源的支持问题**：[brene] 询问是否支持自托管数据源，能否在VPC内运行并直接与RDS实例通信。

data.title: Type-constrained code generation with language models
data.author: tough
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提出了一种利用类型系统约束代码生成的方法，以解决大型语言模型（LLM）在代码生成中频繁出现的类型错误和不可编译问题。作者开发了前缀自动机和可居住类型搜索技术，确保生成的代码符合类型系统的正式规则。该方法在基础类型语言和TypeScript上进行了验证，并在HumanEval和MBPP数据集上的评估显示，编译错误减少了一半以上，代码合成和修复任务中的功能正确性显著提高。该方法适用于不同规模和类型的LLM模型，展示了其通用性和有效性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程语言类型系统和代码生成方面的应用与优化

不同观点：
• [homebrewer] 和 [ArcaneMoose] 认为TypeScript由于拥有丰富的训练数据和类型系统，是LLM理想的应用场景。TypeScript的结构化类型信息可以帮助LLM更准确地生成代码。
• [energy123] 提出了一种策略，即专注于为一种编程语言（尤其是较小或训练数据较少的语言）优化LLM，而不是试图构建一个通用的前沿模型。这种策略可以避免与大厂直接竞争，并满足特定语言的需求。
• [LostBenjamin] 强调了其论文中的方法不仅适用于代码生成，还可以用于代码修复。通过实验证明，这种方法在功能正确性上取得了显著的提升（相对提升37%）。
• [_jayhack_] 提到了MultiLSPy工具，它结合了多个语言服务提供者（LSP），并通过静态分析过滤掉无效的代码结构。这种方法通过超越类型系统的方式进一步优化了代码生成。
• [muglug] 认为大学的研究成果显示出对类型约束等方法的重视，而大厂似乎仍然更倾向于通过扩大模型规模来提升性能。
• [thesz] 质疑类型约束解码方法在像C++和Haskell等语言中的有效性，指出类型推断和复杂依赖关系可能影响该方法的效果。同时提到了Cyc项目的历史，认为当前LLM的许多支持代码其实是在重新发明Cyc。
• [bmc7505] 认为最正确的方法应基于有限模型理论，但目前尚未实现。
• [int19h] 分享了使用Devin工具的经验，指出类型约束在实际应用中的价值，特别是在自动修复代码方面，尽管反馈循环可能较为耗时。
• [kreetx] 建议将该方法扩展到Haskell，并利用Curry-Howard同构性，通过类型签名定义程序，由LLM寻找实现方案。
• [slt2021] 提出是否有可能训练基于AST（抽象语法树）而非token的LLM，以进一步提升代码生成的准确性。
• [_alternator_] 分享了使用Claude代码工具的经验，指出其可以像人类开发者一样，通过迭代修正代码直到编译通过，显示出LLM在实际开发中的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是类型约束方法在不同编程语言中的适用性，尤其是像C++和Haskell这样类型推断和依赖关系复杂的语言。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于反馈循环的效率问题。虽然反馈循环能够提升代码质量，但其时间和计算成本也不容忽视。
• 工具和现有语言服务（如自动导入功能）的整合也被认为是提升LLM应用效果的重要方向。

这些观点共同展示了类型系统和LLM在代码生成和修复中的潜力和挑战，以及不同研究者和实践者对该领域未来发展方向的思考。

Title:
Type-Constrained Code Generation with Language Models
Authors:
Niels Mündler
,
Jingxuan He
,
Hao Wang
,
Koushik Sen
,
Dawn Song
,
Martin Vechev
View a PDF of the paper titled Type-Constrained Code Generation with Language Models, by Niels M\"undler and Jingxuan He and Hao Wang and Koushik Sen and Dawn Song and Martin Vechev
View PDF
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) have achieved notable success in code generation. However, they still frequently produce uncompilable output because their next-token inference procedure does not model formal aspects of code. Although constrained decoding is a promising approach to alleviate this issue, it has only been applied to handle either domain-specific languages or syntactic features of general-purpose programming languages. However, LLMs frequently generate code with typing errors, which are beyond the domain of syntax and generally hard to adequately constrain. To address this challenge, we introduce a type-constrained decoding approach that leverages type systems to guide code generation. For this purpose, we develop novel prefix automata and a search over inhabitable types, forming a sound approach to enforce well-typedness on LLM-generated code. We formalize our approach on a foundational simply-typed language and extend it to TypeScript to demonstrate practicality. Our evaluation on the HumanEval and MBPP datasets shows that our approach reduces compilation errors by more than half and significantly increases functional correctness in code synthesis, translation, and repair tasks across LLMs of various sizes and model families, including state-of-the-art open-weight models with more than 30B parameters. The results demonstrate the generality and effectiveness of our approach in constraining LLM code generation with formal rules of type systems.

• 争议焦点之一是类型约束方法在不同编程语言中的适用性，尤其是像C++和Haskell这样类型推断和依赖关系复杂的语言。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于反馈循环的效率问题。虽然反馈循环能够提升代码质量，但其时间和计算成本也不容忽视。
• 工具和现有语言服务（如自动导入功能）的整合也被认为是提升LLM应用效果的重要方向。

这些观点共同展示了类型系统和LLM在代码生成和修复中的潜力和挑战，以及不同研究者和实践者对该领域未来发展方向的思考。

data.title: Garbage collection of object storage at scale
data.author: ko_pivot
data.article_summary: WarpStream是一个Apache Kafka的替代方案，构建于对象存储之上。其主要技术挑战之一是有效清除已逻辑删除的文件，以避免存储成本过高。简单使用存储桶策略（bucket policy）不适用于复杂系统，如WarpStream，因为它需要支持不同的数据保留期和Kafka的压缩主题功能。同步删除方法也不可行，因为分布式系统中可能出现元数据存储和对象存储不一致的情况，导致文件被遗留在对象存储中，增加成本。为解决此问题，WarpStream考虑使用延迟队列和异步协调等方法来有效管理对象存储的清理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对象存储中的垃圾回收（GC）机制及不同技术方案的优劣

不同观点：
• **DeathAnatos的观点**：不赞同仅依赖桶策略（bucket policy），并提出使用写前日志（WAL, Write-Ahead Log）来处理删除操作。具体做法是将待删除的对象记录到WAL中，执行删除操作后再删除WAL文件。如果系统崩溃，可以根据WAL文件重新执行删除命令。这种方法特别适用于需要在对象存储和SQL数据库等不同存储系统中同步删除操作的场景。

• **Telotortium的观点**：质疑文章的广告性质，指出文章的结构巧妙地将产品宣传融入技术讨论中。该用户提到其公司（WarpStream）销售基于对象存储的Apache Kafka替代品，并认为这种方式比直接在文末打广告更有效。

• **Juancn的观点**：提出了一种基于概率标记-清除（mark-and-sweep）的GC方法，使用布隆过滤器（bloom filter）进行大规模文件/对象的垃圾回收。该方法包括并行构建多个布隆过滤器，然后合并这些过滤器，在清除阶段使用过滤器来判断文件是否仍被引用。布隆过滤器可以确定文件不存活的确定性，而对于可能存活的文件则有一定概率误报。

• **Siscia的观点**：支持使用简单的定期压缩和桶策略结合的方式来进行垃圾回收。具体做法是定期压缩文件，并设置桶策略删除超过一定时间范围的文件。同时设置警报机制监控文件年龄，以确保不会误删仍在使用的文件。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：不同方案在实际应用中的复杂性和可靠性。DeathAnatos强调了WAL的实用性，而Juancn则认为概率性方法（布隆过滤器）更为高效。Siscia则主张简单有效的方案，避免复杂的机制。
• **技术细节**：讨论涉及了多种技术手段，如WAL、布隆过滤器、定期压缩和桶策略等，展示了不同场景下的技术选择和权衡。
• **应用场景**：不同方案适用于不同的成本和可靠性要求，例如Siscia提到的方案在成本不敏感的情况下表现优异。

这些观点展示了在对象存储垃圾回收问题上的多种技术路径和实际考虑。

WarpStream Executive Summary
Sign in
start free
Get started free
HN Disclosure:
WarpStream sells a drop-in replacement for Apache Kafka built directly on-top of object storage.
Over the last 10 years, Iâve built several distributed systems on top of object storage, with
WarpStream
being the most recent. One consistent factor across all of these systems is how much time we spent solving what seems like a relatively straightforward problem: removing files from object storage that had been logically deleted either due to data expiry or compaction.
I discussed this in more detail in
âThe Case for Shared Storageâ blog post
, but to briefly recap: every shared storage system Iâve ever built has looked something like this:
Clients interact with stateless nodes (that are perhaps split into different ârolesâ). The stateless nodes abstract over a shared storage backend (like object storage) and a strongly-consistent metadata store to create some kind of logical abstraction, in WarpStreamâs case: the Apache Kafka protocol.
There are a few ways in which a WarpStream file can end up logically deleted in the metadata store, and therefore needs to be physically deleted from the object store:
All the data in the file has expired due to the configured topic TTLs: â´
All of the data in the file is deleted due to explicit topic deletions: â´
The file was logically deleted by a compaction in which this particular file participated as an input: â´
In the rest of this post, Iâll go over a few different ways to solve this problem by using a
delayed queue
,
async reconciliation
, or
both
. But before I introduce what I think the best ways to solve this problem are, letâs first go over a few approaches that seem obvious, but donât work well in practice like
bucket policies
and
synchronous deletion
.
Why Not Just Use a Bucket Policy?
The easiest way to handle object storage cleanup would be to use a bucket policy with a configurable TTL. For example, we could configure an object storage policy that automatically deletes files that are more than 7 days old. For simple or time-series oriented systems, this is often a good solution.
However, for more complex systems like WarpStream, which has to provide the abstraction of Apache Kafka, this approach doesnât work. For example, consider a WarpStream cluster with hundreds or thousands of different topics. Some topics could be configured with retention as low as 1 hour, and others with retention as high as 90 days. If we relied on a simple bucket policy, then weâd have to configure the bucket policy to be
at least
90 days, which would incur excessive storage costs for the topics with lower retention because a WarpStream file can contain data for many different topics.
Even if we were comfortable with requiring that all topics within a single cluster share a single retention, other implementation details and features in Kafka canât be implemented with a simple object storage bucket policy. For example, Kafka has a feature called âcompacted topicsâ. In a compacted topic, records are deleted / expired not when theyâre too old, but when
theyâre overwritten by a new record with the same key
. A record may be overwritten seconds after it was first written, or several years later.
Unfortunately, bucket policies only work as a mechanism for cleaning up object storage files for the most simple use-cases. Shared storage systems that need to provide more advanced functionality will have to implement object cleanup in the system itself.
Why Not Just Use Synchronous Deletion?
Naively, it seems like whenever the metadata store decides to logically delete a file, it should be able to go and physically remove the file from the object store at the same time, keeping the two systems in sync:
// Tada.
metadataStore.DeleteFile(fileID)
objectStore.DeleteFile(fileID)
â
In traditional programming language theory, this method of garbage collection is analogous to âreference trackingâ. But distributed systems arenât programming languages, and the code above doesnât work in the real world:
if err := metadataStore.DeleteFile(fileID); err != nil {
// This is fine, we can just retry later.
}
if err := objectStore.DeleteFile(fileID); err != nil {
// Uh oh. This file will be orphaned in object storage forever.
}
â
If the file is removed from the metadata store successfully, but isnât removed from the object store (because a node crashed, we got a 500, etc.), then that file will be
orphaned
in the object store.
An orphan file is a file that is physically present in the object store, but not logically tracked in the metadata store, and therefore not part of the distributed database anymore. This is a problem because these orphaned files will accumulate over time and cost you a lot of money.
But actually, thereâs another reason this approach doesnât work even if both deletes succeeded atomically somehow: in-flight queries. The lifecycle of a query in a shared storage s

data.title: Membrane: Media Framework for Elixir
data.author: lawik
data.article_summary: Membrane是一个易于理解和定制的多媒体框架，支持实时通信（WebRTC SFU）、服务器端处理（视频缩放、帧率转换、音频混合等）、多种可切换的输入输出协议（如HLS、RTP、RTSP、RTMP等），并能与Elixir应用无缝集成。它支持多种编解码器的转码，并提供监控工具以帮助调试。该框架由Software Mansion开发，被多家公司用于解决实际问题，如Firework和Keep In Mind。Membrane是开源的，用户可以通过GitHub、Twitter和Discord等平台参与社区并获取支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir中的高性能媒体流框架及其应用和相关资源

不同观点：
• **赞赏项目并强调技术潜力**：
  - [victorbjorklund] 认为该项目很酷，尽管尚未用于严肃项目，但能够在Elixir中拥有高性能的媒体流框架令人惊叹。他提到可以用BEAM构建类似Twitch的应用，尽管建议搭配Postgres数据库。
  - [Sean-Der] 也赞赏项目团队，并提到看到服务器端PeerConnection统计可视化和视频合成器的实时修改功能，认为这是未来的技术。

• **寻求学习资源和教程**：
  - [kingofheroes] 提到以前做过Phoenix框架的教程并享受其中，询问是否有好的最新教程推荐。

• **对许可证问题的关注**：
  - [AlphaWeaver] 提到在为客户项目考虑使用该框架时，发现部分组件使用自定义许可证，尽管大部分是Apache 2.0开源许可证，但需要注意选择合适的部分使用。

• **对技术选择的遗憾**：
  - [mml] 表示希望Nvidia选择这个方向而不是gstreamer，暗示对gstreamer技术选择的不满。

• **对项目需求的表达**：
  - [neya] 认为Elixir非常需要这样的项目，过去常被迫使用NodeJS实现，对此项目表示感谢。

• **开发环境体验**：
  - [nw05678] 表示在探索Elixir时，发现其开发环境不如其他语言流畅。

补充讨论：
- 该项目被广泛认为具有很大潜力，尤其在Elixir生态系统中提供了高性能媒体流的能力。
- 用户对项目的技术实现和团队表示赞赏，但也有人对开发环境和许可证问题表示关注。
- 学习资源的需求和不同技术选择的对比也是讨论中的重要部分。

43945483.article_content:
your multimedia
solution
An easily understandable and customisable multimedia framework.
What can you do with Membrane?
Real Time Communication
WebRTC SFU implementation with modular architecture for custom I/O. Perfect for applying processing, dumping media at any stage, or creating additional non-WebRTC outputs.
Server-side processing
Video scaling, framerate conversion, cut & merge and text overlay. Audio mixing, resampling and fading. With easy option to create and add custom ones.
Multiple and switchable I/O protocols
Existing implementations of WebRTC, HLS, RTP, RTSP, RTMP, File, Http chunks, integration with speech to text utilities.
Seamless integration with any Elixir app
Membrane is built in Elixir. It reaps the benefits of Elixir's scalability and fault tolerance. But also because of that Mebrane's pipelines can easily become a part of any Elixir application, e.g. a web server built with Phoenix.
Transcoding
From and to many popular codecs: aac, opus, mpeg, h264, vp9, vp8.
Monitoring utilities
Tools to monitor pipeline health and EVM performance to ease debugging process.
Trusted by

data.title: Fingers wrinkle the same way every time they’re in the water too long
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了宾厄姆顿大学副教授Guy German及其团队的一项研究，他们发现长时间泡水后手指皱纹的形成是由于皮肤下血管收缩，而非此前认为的皮肤吸水膨胀。研究还解答了一个孩子提出的问题：每次泡水后，手指皱纹的形态是否一致？通过实验，他们证明了皱纹的形态在多次泡水后保持一致，因为血管的相对位置较为固定。此外，研究还发现手指正中神经损伤的人不会出现皱纹。这项研究不仅解答了一个有趣的问题，还可能在法医学中应用于指纹识别等领域。
